resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' inferable (not literal). Egypt Oil & Gas 'The Western Desert' report lists Tarek-Ameryia in its live 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table (13 existing WD gas pipelines) and the companion feature calls it 'the biggest of the Western Desert pipelines' (present tense, existing). OGJ independently confirms the fed Western Desert Gas Complex at El-Amreya is currently processing 950 MMcfd of Western Desert gas, so the feeder is in service. Two independent origins support operating.

Egypt Oil & Gas WD report table lists Tarek-Ameryia Capacity = 950 mmcf/d exactly (matches sheet 950.00 MMcf/d). OGJ independently states the Western Desert Gas Complex at El-Amreya, which this pipeline feeds, currently processes 950 MMcfd (pre-Train-D). Note the OGJ 950 is the receiving complex's throughput, not a pipeline-specific figure, but it is consistent with and corroborates the pipeline capacity. Two independent origins agree on 950.

Egypt Oil & Gas WD report table gives Tarek-Ameryia Length = 231 km (matches sheet 231.00 km); the companion Egypt Oil & Gas distribution feature repeats 'total length of 231 km'. Both are the same publisher (Egypt Oil & Gas), so treat as one strong origin -> medium. CONTRADICTION to flag: an older OGJ account describes the original Shell/Repsol Obaiyed->Ameriya line as ~315 km; the 315 km figure likely reflects a different/earlier routing (or the full gathering run) vs the 231 km trunk figure now reported. Could not corroborate 231 km from a second independent origin.

Egypt Oil & Gas WD report table gives Tarek-Ameryia Diameter = 34 inches (matches sheet 34.00 in). Single-origin (only Egypt Oil & Gas carries the diameter); no independent second source found for diameter -> medium.

Egypt Oil & Gas WD report lists this line From 'Tarek' To 'Ameryia' (Tarek is a Khalda field in the Western Desert), matching sheet Start=Western Desert / End=Ameryia. OGJ independently places the receiving Western Desert Gas Complex in El-Amreya, Alexandria and identifies its feed fields as Al-Obayed (BAPETCO) and Salam/Tarek/El-Qaser (Khalda) in the Western Desert - corroborating both endpoints (WD fields -> Ameryia, Alexandria). Two independent origins agree.

No source found supporting Owner1 = 'General Petroleum Co' (GPC) for this pipeline. CONTRADICTION to flag: the Amreya (El-Amreya) receiving complex and the northern WD gas grid are operated by GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Co; shareholders EGAS 70% / Egypt Gas 15% / Petrojet 15%, per OGJ), while the feed fields are operated by BAPETCO (Obayed) and Khalda (Tarek/Salam) - none of these is GPC. GPC's documented Western Desert gas pipeline is the separate first-phase Abu Sennan line in the SOUTHERN Western Desert (Future Pipe Industries delivery, 24 km), not the northern Tarek-Ameryia trunk. The GPC=100% attribution appears misassigned and should be reviewed by Update rather than given a fabricated ref.
